findings.observation: Sheet 3 contains extensive Austin Energy transmission easement coordination notes with requirements for 25-foot clearances, grading coordination, fencing coordination, and pre-construction safety meetings. Specific contact information for Andrew Perez (512-505-7153) is provided for grading coordination and pre-construction meetings. However, the transmission easement is NOT depicted on Sheet 9 (Site Plan) or Sheet 21 (Electrical Design Plan). The site plan shows multiple electric easements (5', 15' widths) but no transmission easement boundary is drawn. No formal Austin Energy Transmission review approval stamp, letter, or documentation is visible on the electrical design or site plan sheets.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.14.0 requires transmission facility review by Austin Energy for clearances, access, and maintenance. The project contains transmission easements (evidenced by notes on Sheet 3), yet the transmission easement boundary is not depicted on the site plan sheets where it is needed for design coordination. The site plan lacks visual representation of the transmission easement, making it impossible to verify that proposed improvements (buildings, utilities, grading, fencing) comply with the 25-foot clearance requirements and other transmission protection measures. While coordination notes are present on Sheet 3, there is no evidence on the actual site plan sheets that Austin Energy Transmission has reviewed and approved the electrical design, site plan layout, or equipment placement relative to transmission facilities.
findings.comment: Transmission easement not depicted on site plan sheets. Add transmission easement boundary to site plans with dimensions and coordinates. Obtain and submit Austin Energy Transmission engineering review approval documenting clearance verification for all proposed improvements relative to transmission structures and easement requirements.

findings.observation: No transmission easement is shown on the site plans (Sheets 9 and 21), therefore no CAD overlay showing building footprints relative to transmission line easement can be verified. Multiple electric easements are labeled (5', 15' widths) on the property perimeter, but the transmission easement boundary is not depicted. Without the transmission easement depicted and building footprints overlaid, accurate clearance measurement cannot be performed.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.14.0 requires CAD files showing building footprint overlaid on transmission easement for accurate clearance verification when buildings encroach into easements. The absence of the transmission easement on the plans prevents verification of clearances. While this site shows electric easements, the transmission easement referenced in Sheet 3 coordination notes is not depicted, making it impossible to verify that buildings maintain required clearances from transmission structures.
findings.comment: Provide CAD file showing plan view of all building footprints overlaid on transmission line easement boundary with dimensions showing distances from transmission structures. Coordinate with Austin Energy to verify clearance compliance.

applicableAreas: Southern property boundary near overhead electric line
findings.observation: Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) shows trees planted along the southern boundary of the property in proximity to an overhead electric (OHE) line. The landscaping plan includes multiple tree planting symbols (large circles) positioned near this overhead electric facility. However, there are no clearance zone notations, no warnings, and no indication that Austin Energy transmission reviewer approval was obtained for this landscaping plan. No documentation of AE transmission review or approval is provided.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.14.0 requires landscaping in transmission areas to be approved by Austin Energy transmission reviewer. Sheet 3 transmission notes explicitly state: 'No trees shall be planted within the transmission easement. No trees shall be planted within 25 feet of the base of the transmission structure.' The landscape plan shows tree plantings without documented compliance with these clearances or AE approval. Trees planted within clearance zones pose safety hazards and violate transmission protection requirements.
findings.comment: Landscaping in transmission areas not approved by AE transmission reviewer. Revise landscape plan to remove trees from transmission easement and 25-foot clearance zones around transmission structures. Obtain Austin Energy transmission reviewer approval of final landscape plan demonstrating compliance with 25-foot clearance requirements.

findings.observation: Sheet 9 and Sheet 31 show wooden privacy fencing running along the eastern and northern property boundaries. The eastern fencing is located directly within or immediately adjacent to electric easements labeled on Sheet 9 as 'Electric Easement Vol. 69, Pg. 14' and on Sheet 11 as '15' Electric Easement Vol. 73, Pg. 76.' No license agreement documentation is included in the provided site plan materials for improvements (fencing) located within AE easements.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.10 requires license agreements for landscaping, trees, encroachments, or construction activities within AE easements. Agreements must be reviewed and approved by both AE Property Agents and AE Design prior to site plan approval. Fencing is an encroachment within an AE easement. No evidence of a license agreement has been submitted with this site plan application.
findings.comment: License agreement not submitted for fencing within AE electric easement. Submit license agreement reviewed and approved by Austin Energy Property Agents and AE Design prior to site plan approval. Agreement must address fencing maintenance, easement access provisions, and removal obligations if AE requires future access.

applicableAreas: Eastern, northern, and southern property boundaries
findings.observation: Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) shows wooden privacy fencing (H-6 symbol) running along the northern, eastern, and southern property boundaries. The sheet contains only the symbol callouts and legend definitions but provides NO construction details such as fence height, materials specifications, post spacing, footing depths, or assembly details. No reference is made to detail sheets or section drawings for the fence construction.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0 requires construction details of fences when fencing is proposed near AE facilities. The fencing shown on this plan is in proximity to electric easements (Sheet 9 labels 'Electric Easement Vol. 69, Pg. 14' and Sheet 11 shows '15' Electric Easement Vol. 73, Pg. 76'). Construction details are essential for AE Design to review and approve the fence installation method to ensure it does not damage or interfere with underlying utilities or easement access.
findings.comment: Construction details of fence not provided. Submit detailed fence construction drawings showing materials, dimensions, post spacing, footing details, and gate locations. Details must show fence design is compatible with AE easement access and clearance requirements.

findings.observation: Sheet 31 shows wooden privacy fencing at the property boundaries but contains only plan-view callouts. No profile plan or section drawings are provided showing the vertical relationship between the fence line and the underlying electric easement or utility facilities. Sheet 9 identifies that the eastern fencing is located within electric easement areas. No documentation indicates that AE Design has reviewed and provided preliminary approval of the fence/utility coordination.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0 requires profile plan and detail drawings of fence and existing utility facilities be provided for AE Design review and preliminary approval when fence installation may affect or be near existing AE utilities. The fence shown is in electric easement areas (Sheet 9: 'Electric Easement Vol. 69, Pg. 14'; Sheet 11: '15' Electric Easement Vol. 73, Pg. 76'). Profile plans showing vertical clearances and utility coordination are necessary for AE Design to confirm the fence design will not interfere with easement access or damage underlying facilities.
findings.comment: Profile plan and detail drawings of fence and existing utility facilities not provided for AE Design review. Submit fence profile sections and coordination drawings showing fence elevation relative to electric easement boundaries and any existing utilities. Obtain Austin Energy Design preliminary approval of fence installation method.

applicableAreas: Dead-end access for emergency and utility vehicles
findings.observation: Sheet 9 (Site Plan) shows internal drive aisles with two permanent driveway entrances on the western property line. The eastern drive aisle extends into the site to service Buildings 3-6 but terminates in a dead-end configuration at a curb and gutter line with a retaining wall beyond. No labeled or graphically defined turnaround area (hammerhead, T-turn, cul-de-sac, or other turning radius) is shown for vehicles to turn around or exit. The sheet provides no information about AE truck access requirements or vehicle turnaround capability.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.3.16 requires that all AE facilities have truck access with the ability to turn around or exit the property. The site has four transformer pads (shown on Sheet 21) that require periodic maintenance and service access by Austin Energy vehicles. The dead-end eastern drive aisle does not provide the AE vehicles with ability to turn around or exit efficiently. This violates the truck access turnaround requirement.
findings.comment: AE vehicle turnaround or exit capability not provided. Revise site plan to provide a turnaround area (hammerhead, T-turn, or cul-de-sac) at the eastern drive aisle terminus with minimum dimensions per UCM § 1.3.16 (minimum 20 feet × 35 feet set-up area with 35 feet vertical clearance for AE vehicles). Show AE truck access routing and confirm turn-around capability.

findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows 'Electrical Meters' labeled on the exteriors of the eight buildings (noted near units 102/103, 201/202, 301/302, 401/402, 501/502, 603, 701/702, 801/802). However, 'Electrical Disconnects' are NOT explicitly labeled or identified anywhere on the sheet. No dimension lines or distance measurements are shown between the meter locations and any disconnect locations. No distance verification is possible to confirm meters and disconnects are grouped together or that separation does not exceed the 20-foot maximum. Pull boxes are shown but cannot be confirmed as disconnects.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.9.3.1(I) requires that meters and disconnects be grouped together in a common location with maximum 20-foot separation and within line of sight. Sheet 21 shows meters but does not identify disconnects as distinct labeled elements. Without both meters and disconnects identified and dimensioned, compliance with the grouping, separation distance, and line-of-sight requirements cannot be verified. The applicant has not provided sufficient detail to demonstrate compliance.
findings.comment: Meters and disconnects not grouped together with documented separation distance. Identify and label all electrical disconnects on the site plan. Show distance measurements between meters and disconnects, documenting that separation does not exceed 20 feet and that meters and disconnects are within line of sight. Verify grouping in common location per UCM § 1.9.3.1(I).

applicableAreas: Middle areas adjacent to drive aisles
findings.observation: Sheet 21 shows four transformer pads (dashed rectangles) at locations middle-left (west of Bldg 1), bottom-left (west of Bldg 8), middle-right (between Bldgs 4-5), and bottom-right (between Bldgs 6-7). Sheet 9 (Site Plan) shows these transformer pads immediately adjacent to internal drive aisles (parking and traffic areas). No bollards, protective barriers, or any protective posts are shown around any of the transformer pad locations. No callouts or notes reference bollard requirements.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.4 requires 4-inch minimum galvanized rigid metal posts (bollards) per AE Design equipment pad details when pad-mounted equipment is within 4 feet of parking or traffic areas. The transformer pads shown on Sheet 9 are positioned directly adjacent to internal drive aisles and parking areas, placing them well within the 4-foot proximity threshold. The absence of bollards on all four transformer pads is a deficiency. Bollards are essential to protect pad-mounted transformers from vehicle damage.
findings.comment: Bollards not shown when equipment pads are within 4 feet of parking/traffic areas. Add 4-inch minimum galvanized rigid metal bollards around each transformer pad per Austin Energy Design equipment pad details. Show bollard locations and spacing on site plan with reference to AE Design standard details.

findings.observation: Sheet 21 shows four transformer pad locations. Sheet 11 (Grading Plan) does not identify or label any transformer pads. No spot elevations, drainage flow arrows, or grading notes are shown around transformer pad locations on the Grading Plan. No elevation data is provided for the transformer pads themselves. The grading plan shows general site topography and contour lines (680, 682, etc.) but does not specifically address drainage direction or protection requirements around the electrical equipment.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.4 (footnote 1) requires that grading and drainage direction around oil-filled pad-mounted equipment be designed to flow away from buildings. The grading plan must identify transformer locations, show spot elevations for pads, and indicate drainage flow direction with arrows to confirm water is directed away from equipment. The absence of transformer pad identification and drainage notation on the Grading Plan prevents verification of compliance with drainage requirements. This is a critical oversight as improper drainage toward transformers can cause damage and environmental contamination.
findings.comment: Grading/drainage direction around oil-filled pad-mounted equipment not designed or documented. Identify all transformer pad locations on Grading Plan. Show spot elevations for each transformer pad and surrounding terrain. Add drainage flow arrows demonstrating that grading slopes and surface water flow direct water away from transformer pads per UCM § 1.10.4. Provide drainage design calculations or notes confirming compliance.

findings.observation: Sheet 3 contains Austin Energy transmission notes requiring: 'A pre-construction safety meeting is required with Austin Energy 48 hours before commencement of construction. Call Andrew Perez at 512 505 7153 to schedule a tailgate safety meeting.' This requirement is clearly documented on the plans. However, no documentation, meeting minutes, confirmation letter, or other evidence is provided in the submitted site plan materials indicating that this required pre-construction safety meeting with Austin Energy Transmission has been scheduled or completed.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.14.0 requires a Notice of Electrical Hazard meeting with Austin Energy Transmission Construction & Maintenance before demolition begins (when demolition or grading near transmission structures is proposed). While this site plan document shows the requirement for a pre-construction safety meeting on Sheet 3, the site plan application materials do not include evidence that the meeting has been scheduled or held. Without documentation of compliance with this pre-construction coordination requirement, it cannot be verified that the project is proceeding safely with proper AE Transmission awareness.
findings.comment: Notice of Electrical Hazard meeting with AE Transmission Construction & Maintenance not documented. Schedule and conduct pre-construction safety meeting with Austin Energy Transmission (Contact: Andrew Perez 512-505-7153; Chuck Hendry 505-7151 if cranes used) at least 48 hours before construction begins. Submit meeting confirmation documentation with grading and demolition permit applications.

findings.observation: The site plan and facts show multiple overlapping utility easements: (1) Austin Energy electric easements (5', 15' widths) shown on Sheets 9 and 11; (2) City of Austin drainage easement (0.130 acres, NE corner of site per facts.md); (3) Austin Water wastewater and water easements. Sheet 3 contains extensive Austin Energy transmission easement coordination requirements. However, no inter-departmental agreement or MOU between Austin Energy and other city departments (such as Austin Water Watershed Protection or Public Works) is evident in the submitted materials documenting how overlapping easement requirements will be managed.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.14.0 requires inter-departmental agreement or MOU when transmission easements or facilities overlap with other department jurisdictions. While the facts show multiple city departments have interests (Austin Energy, Austin Water, City Watershed Protection), no documentation is provided showing coordination agreements, MOUs, or formal communication between departments. Overlapping easements create complex access and maintenance scenarios that require formal inter-agency coordination.
findings.comment: Inter-departmental agreement or MOU not obtained between AE and other city departments regarding overlapping easement requirements. Submit inter-departmental agreement or MOU between Austin Energy, Austin Water, and City Watershed Protection Department addressing transmission easement and drainage easement overlaps. Agreement must clarify access rights, maintenance responsibilities, and emergency protocols.

findings.observation: Sheet 3 includes approval letters from Austin Water confirming adequate capacity for water and wastewater service. The facts show a City of Austin drainage easement (0.130 acres) on the site. However, the Austin Water approval documentation on Sheet 3 does not explicitly address coordination of water/wastewater easements with overlapping Austin Energy electric easements. The coordination between Austin Water and Austin Energy utilities is not documented beyond the general approvals.
findings.reasoning: When Austin Water and Austin Energy easements overlap, explicit coordination is necessary to address access, maintenance, and potential conflicts. The facts show both utilities have interests on this site, but the submitted materials do not demonstrate that Austin Water and Austin Energy have coordinated their respective requirements. While Austin Water has provided service capacity approval, coordination regarding overlapping easement impacts is not evident.
findings.comment: Austin Water approval not explicitly documented for overlapping easement coordination with Austin Energy easements. Submit confirmation from Austin Water that water/wastewater service plans have been coordinated with Austin Energy regarding overlapping or adjacent easement requirements and construction impacts.

findings.observation: Sheet 9 (Site Plan) shows two permanent driveways on the western property line labeled 'Construct Type II Driveway' and 'Construct Type III Driveway.' These are the only vehicle access points shown to the site. However, a temporary stabilized construction entrance is not specifically labeled or depicted as a distinct feature on the site plan. The permanent driveways pass through multiple easements (Sidewalk Easement, Wastewater Easement, 12' Water Line Vault Easement) but do not explicitly cross Austin Energy property or electric easements at these points. The construction entrance location and whether it's on AE property is unclear from the available plans.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0 requires that if a proposed construction entrance is located on AE property, it must be relocated within the limits of construction of the site plan. The site plan does not show a distinct temporary construction entrance feature, and the relationship of the permanent driveways to Austin Energy property is not clearly documented. Without clear labeling and location confirmation, it cannot be verified whether the construction entrance complies with this requirement.
findings.comment: Proposed construction entrance location not clearly shown on site plan. If a temporary stabilized construction entrance is required for construction access, clearly label its location on the site plan and confirm it does not encroach on Austin Energy property. If located on AE property, relocate within limits of construction. Provide documentation of construction entrance location relative to AE easement boundaries.

findings.observation: Sheet 10 (Fire Protection Plan) shows internal drive aisles serving the eight buildings with fire lanes, but does not explicitly label any routes as passing through an Austin Energy transmission easement. Sheet 9 shows internal driveways but the transmission easement is not depicted, making it unclear whether fire lanes/driveways technically pass through the transmission easement area or merely adjacent to it. The site plan lacks clear visualization of the transmission easement boundary relative to fire lane routing.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.0 requires that if a fire lane routing crosses AE property, it must be relocated within limits of construction and necessary clearances must be met. Without the transmission easement boundary depicted on the site plan, it cannot be verified whether fire lanes pass through the easement or maintain required clearances. Sheet 3 transmission notes indicate 25-foot clearances are required from transmission structures, but the actual easement boundaries are not shown for comparison against fire lane locations.
findings.comment: Proposed fire lane routing relative to AE transmission easement not clearly documented. Depict transmission easement boundary on site plan and verify that fire lane routing does not cross the easement or, if it must cross, confirm it is relocated within construction limits and maintains all required clearances per UCM § 1.10.0 and Sheet 3 transmission easement requirements (25-foot clearance from structures, 46,000 lb pavement design in easement).

findings.observation: Sheets 15 and 16 show a biofiltration/detention pond located in the northeast portion of the site. Sheet 9 shows the pond adjacent to the eastern property boundary where electric easements are located. Sheets 15-16 contain engineering details for the pond including stage-storage calculations, material specifications, and drainage infrastructure. However, there is no documentation showing that Austin Energy has been consulted or has approved the pond design relative to impacts on electrical facilities, easement access, or utility protection. No coordination notes between the drainage design and electrical facility protection are evident.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.0 requires that electric facilities conflicts with proposed ponds and water features be resolved per AE criteria. While the pond design is well-documented in engineering terms, there is no evidence of Austin Energy review or approval of potential conflicts between pond construction/operations and electrical facility access or protection. The pond location adjacent to electrical easements may impact AE maintenance access or require special protection measures during pond construction.
findings.comment: Electric facilities conflicts with proposed ponds and water features not resolved per AE criteria. Submit documentation showing Austin Energy Design review and approval of detention pond design relative to protection of electrical facilities and easement access. Address any required clearances, protective measures, or operational constraints related to electrical utilities adjacent to the pond.

findings.observation: Sheet 3 contains comprehensive transmission and substation requirements per UCM § 1.14.0 with detailed notes on easement clearances, access provisions, grading restrictions, fencing coordination, and construction protocols. However, examination of Sheets 9, 11, and 21 (Site Plan, Grading Plan, and Electrical Design Plan) reveals that the transmission easement is NOT depicted on these working sheets. The transmission easement boundary is not shown on the site or grading plans where it is essential for design coordination. Transformer pads are shown but are not correlated with transmission easement requirements. The site plan layout does not explicitly demonstrate compliance with transmission easement requirements through visual representation.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.14.0 Transmission and Substation Requirements mandate that sites with transmission facilities must follow specific design and coordination protocols. While the general notes on Sheet 3 reference these requirements, the actual site plan sheets do not demonstrate compliance through proper depiction of the transmission easement, clearance zones, and design accommodations. The transmission easement must be depicted on the working plans with dimensions and coordinates so that all designers (landscape, grading, electrical, site) can coordinate their work to maintain required clearances and access provisions.
findings.comment: Site plan not following UCM § 1.14.0 Transmission and Substation Requirements - transmission easement not depicted on working plans. Add transmission easement boundary to all relevant site plan sheets (Site Plan, Grading Plan, Electrical Design Plan) with dimensions and coordinates. Show 25-foot clearance zones from transmission structures. Demonstrate compliance with all transmission easement requirements on the plans, not just in general notes.
